newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenian Salus sags 10 pct in early trade.
newsitem.headline: Slovenian Salus sags 10 pct in early trade.

text.p: Slovenian pharmaceutical wholesaler Salus dropped nearly ten percent in early trade on Tuesday for the third day in a row as a result of the company's privatisation problems, brokers said.
At 0830 GMT Salus was down 9.85 percent at 12,170 tolars from Monday's close of 13,500 tolars.

"Salus could fall to about 10,000 tolars by the end of April because it recently became clear that it would take at least another year before the court case regarding its privatisation is over," said Zoran Spasenic, a trader of brokerage BPH.

In February last year the Payment Agency ordered Salus to introduce an 80-percent state stake in the company claiming it incorrectly transferred state capital to its newly established subsidiary Finsa in 1990 and 1991.
The case went to court after Salus, which is 100-percent privately owned, refused to alter its ownership.
Salus last week announced the court proceedings were continuing without any major results so far.

Traders said Salus was unlikely to fall below 10,000 tolars in the near future because of its relatively good business results but added the share could slump significantly if the court would decide Salus would have to alter its ownership.
The company said earlier its 1996 net profit fell to 457.5 million tolars from 491.9 million while sales rose to 10.34 billion tolars from 9.25 billion.
